assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theory prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated-insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moire quantum matter as a new tunable platform. The pairing of a clear prediction with a nature-led surprise is the kind of discovery-centred case I find most persuasive.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero led the decisive 2018 experiments. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment triple within the supplied names. Credit for the earlier twisted-graphene theory and for the Cory Dean/Philip Kim-type device lineage is not in the supplied credit and may need weighing.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories with rapidly growing follow-on science (fractional Chern insulators, moire excitons). The field is young, so the long-term lasting impact is still being established, but the core discovery is robust.
uncertainties: Whether the field is mature enough or the prize would be premature relative to the eventual fate of the superconducting mechanism.
Unresolved credit for other theory precursors and for experimental groups with parallel observations; I have not independently verified the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new classification of electronic phases of matter, with a clean theoretical idea confirmed in precise experiments. Conceptually deep and broadly influential, extending beyond 2016 topological-phase recognition.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall insulator in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied names allow a coherent triple, but Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu are not within the credited names, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent experiments (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, 3D materials by ARPES). Recognition is timely to somewhat overdue; the 2016 prize treated topological phase transitions but not this line.
uncertainties: Contested allocation among the many theorists (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu) who fall outside the supplied names.
The B002 candidate is overlapping and would bring different credit; I have not independently verified priority questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, with later evidence from TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy and is a discovery of nature rather than a model. This is the sort of new window onto the cosmos that I take most seriously.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Karle and Spiering are credited for central instrumental and collaboration leadership. The supplied triple is plausible, but large-collaboration discoveries make individual allocation difficult, and AMANDA/Baikal precursors involve other people.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by multiple IceCube analyses and partially by other detectors; source identification is still partial, so the interpretation of origins is not fully settled. Reasonably timely given the Galactic-plane result.
uncertainties: Source population and production mechanisms remain open, so the interpretive maturity is incomplete.
Credit within a thousand-person collaboration and relative roles of precursors; I have not verified these independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, deliver unprecedented fractional uncertainty and stability, enable relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants, and reach the frontier of precision physics. Clear invention with clear impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice clock, and Ye's group brought it to the lowest systematic uncertainties and many-body-limited operation. A two-person award is clean, with Hall and Haensch having already been recognised in 2005 for the comb.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely reproduced in several laboratories, and moving toward a redefinition of the second. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Relationship to the 2005 and 2012 prizes might make the Committee reluctant to reward a further precision-metrology case.
Contributions of other lattice-clock groups (e.g. Ludlow, Lemke) are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* directly test strong-field gravity and black-hole accretion, giving a visual confirmation of the near-horizon region. As a black-hole physicist I find the science compelling, and the observational result is clear and original in method.
assessment.attribution: The result is a product of a large collaboration. Doeleman led the EHT project, Falcke proposed imaging the shadow and Zensus built the VLBI base; this is a defensible triple but heavily simplifies a collective achievement, and the Nobel rule of three people strains here.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged and consistent with general relativity, with polarisation results; however, precision tests of gravity from the images are still limited, and the black-hole prize in 2020 already covered much of the area.
uncertainties: Attribution within a very large collaboration is a real obstacle.
Limited test precision of general relativity so far; I cannot independently verify the interpretation of the images beyond the supplied description.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed trapped-ion quantum computing and later, with Bloch and others, the controlled-atom approach to quantum simulation. Conceptually important and widely influential across atomic physics and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the central theoretical authors; Bloch is the leading optical-lattice experimentalist; Blatt realised many ion-trap gates. The supplied list has four names but only three may be selected, and the overlap with B041 and B043 (same theorists) complicates which framing is right.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for ions and atoms, with real devices operating, but practical impact on large-scale computation is still unfolding. 2012 and 2025 prizes already covered related ground, which affects timing.
uncertainties: Overlap with other candidates carrying the same names and the exclusion of Blatt under a three-person limit.
Whether the prize would be seen as recognising quantum-information concepts rather than a single decisive discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of the baryon acoustic peak in galaxy clustering gave a robust standard ruler for the expansion history and became a pillar of precision cosmology and dark-energy constraints, a topic close to my own interests. Recent hints from DESI of possible evolving dark energy add urgency, though that interpretation is unsettled.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein et al. (SDSS) and Cole et al. (2dFGRS), with Peacock's role in 2dFGRS, give a plausible triple, but the two surveys were collaborations, and Percival and others are not credited; allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: The BAO feature is firmly confirmed by many surveys. Its fundamental interpretation is well understood, but the cosmological prize may seem to overlap with 2011 (accelerating expansion) and 2019.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier cosmology prizes and ambiguous credit between two survey collaborations.
DESI evolving dark-energy hints are not settled and I do not rely on them for ranking.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson at the LHC confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking in the Standard Model and was an experimental triumph. It is nature-confirmed, central and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised Englert and Higgs. The experimental discovery is credited to the ATLAS and CMS collaborations; the supplied names are leaders and spokespersons, and selecting three of four of them is arbitrary relative to the thousands of contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with properties of the Higgs measured in detail. Timing is late relative to the discovery, and the prize committee has avoided collaboration awards since 2013.
uncertainties: Attribution to individuals for a collaboration-scale discovery is deeply unresolved, and omitting Della Negra is a judgement I cannot justify scientifically.
Whether the Committee would revisit the Higgs after 2013; I have not independently verified prior Committee practice.
